title: Priority handoff and burst-window routing for tiered plans with quota-aware regional fallbacks
creator: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary:
Implement a tier-aware routing handoff that gives short burst windows to lower-tier requests while preserving enterprise throughput guarantees. The system should be quota-aware at the tenant level, use regional affinity for latency-sensitive traffic, and have automatic fallback to lighter-weight model variants when capacity thresholds are reached.

Goals:
- Preserve enterprise SLAs under bursty load from free/paid plans.
- Allow short, predictable bursts for free/paid users without impacting paid customers’ p95 SLOs.
- Provide deterministic fallback to smaller/quantized model variants when regional pools are saturated.
- Expose routing decisions and fairness metrics in Console for ops and SRE.

Non-goals:
- Global capacity rebalancing (outside scope for Phase 2).
- Long-tail fairness reallocation; we focus on short (seconds-to-minutes) bursts.

Design (proposal):
1) Burst windows (soft handoff):
   - Each tenant receives a token-bucket-style short-term burst allowance (burst_window_tokens) sized by plan class: free=10 tokens/60s, paid=50 tokens/60s, enterprise=200 tokens/60s (values tunable).
   - Tokens are consumed per-request using a cost model (tokens per unit work). When tokens are available, requests are admitted to the normal low-latency lane.
   - When tokens are exhausted, requests are demoted to a ‘grace window’ lane which has slower admission and reduced throughput but still attempts low-latency handling for paid/enterprise.

2) Priority handoff thresholds and decay:
   - Define two thresholds per regional pool: soft_capacity and critical_capacity. When regional active load exceeds soft_capacity, free plan requests are probabilistically demoted based on token exhaustion and age of burst. When critical_capacity is hit, paid plan requests are gradually demoted in favor of enterprise until enterprise SLOs are met.
   - Handoff decisions include an exponential backoff decay so tenants that hit demotion recover faster if activity subsides.

3) Regional affinity + spillover policy:
   - Requests prefer region-affine pools. If local region hit soft_capacity and burst tokens are available, prefer local admission. If local region is saturated beyond critical_capacity, spillover to nearest region (latency penalty) or fallback to quantized model variants in-region. Spillover policy uses tenant routing preferences and customer tier.

4) Fallback model variants:
   - Define model variants (full, quantized-small, quantized-xsmall) with known performance/cost profiles. In saturation, route lower-tier traffic to a quantized variant if available for that model family. Enterprise traffic should only fallback to a compatible enterprise-grade variant.

5) Cost and SLO accounting:
   - Track per-tenant admission, demotion counts, model-variant usage, and p50/p95/p99 latency per plan. Create fairness metric: (service_level_violation_rate_by_tier) and cost_delta_by_tier.

Telemetry & Observability:
- Console dashboards: routing-handoff, burst-token-consumption, regional-spillover, fallback-variant-usage.
- Alert rules: enterprise p95 > SLO for 2m -> trigger emergency demotion rollback and auto-scale.
- Sampling: store request-level decision traces for 0.1% of requests for recent 72h for postmortem.

Testing & Validation:
- Unit tests for token-bucket accounting, decay/backoff, and threshold math.
- Integration test harness: synthetic tenant generator to simulate bursts at different tiers and regions.
- Load test: run chaos scenarios: regional saturation, instance loss, and cold-cache model swaps.

Rollout plan:
1) Internal rollout to Canary cluster with feature flag (routing.v2.priority_handoff) and per-tenant opt-in.
2) Monitor key metrics for 72 hours: enterprise p95/p99, paid p95, fairness metric.
3) Gradual ramp to 10% customers, then 50%, with cutover control and immediate rollback on threshold breaches.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Token sizing: fixed windows vs adaptive sizing based on historical burst patterns. (PM prefers adaptive; complexity trade-off.)
- Demotion signal sources: rely purely on real-time regional occupancy or incorporate predictive signals from autoscaler forecasts.
- Whether to bill fallback-variant cost differently for paid tiers (needs pricing/Finance input).

Implementation notes / references:
- Related design doc: https://confluence.redwood/inference/SmartRouting/PriorityHandoff (draft)
- Prototype PR (kernel + routing): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
- Console dashboard draft: https://console.redwood/inference/dashboards/routing-fairness
- Simulation scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sim-tools/pull/112

Progress updates (chronological):
- 2026-02-10: Ticket created by Ava Martinez. Initial scoping and doc links.
- 2026-02-17: Design review with PM (Elena Kaur) and SRE. Decision: use token-bucket burst windows for Phase 2. Action: ENG to prototype accounting in admission controller.
- 2026-02-25: Prototype PR opened by Ravi (PR 4821). Basic token accounting in admission controller + experiment flag. Tests added.
- 2026-03-02: Internal load test: token parameters too lenient for free tier — increased free token refill tuning and added decay. Updated config in runtime-1.23 branch.
- 2026-03-05: UX/Console stub added for visibility; initial metrics surfaced to staging Console.
- 2026-03-10: Security review kickoff. SRE raised audit logging requirements for demotion decisions; added as dependency for release.
- 2026-03-12: Canary rollout scheduled; current status: In Progress.

Review feedback (summarized):
- PM (Elena Kaur): Favor adaptive token sizing; approved Phase 2 static approach for faster rollout.
- SRE (Mateo Li): Requires additional audit logs for automated demotion and a playbook for rollback. Added to dependencies.
- Design (Priya Shah): Console needs an explanation panel for tenants that were recently demoted; assigned to DevEx.

Next actions (assigned):
- Ravi Patel: finish PR42 for demotion audit logs and integrate with observability hooks (due 2026-03-16).
- Ava Martinez: finalize rollout checklist and post-canary metrics (due 2026-03-18).
- Elena Kaur (PM): coordinate pricing/finance for fallback variant billing decision (due 2026-03-25).

Links to artifacts: 
- Design doc (draft): https://confluence.redwood/inference/SmartRouting/PriorityHandoff
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
- Simulation repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sim-tools/pull/112
- Console Dashboard (staging): https://console.redwood/inference/dashboards/routing-fairness

Notes for reviewers: please focus on the handoff math in section 1 and the rollback triggers under Rollout plan. If we accept adaptive sizing for Phase 2, the implementation estimate moves to 8 points and the schedule slips by ~3 weeks.
